description: `rlsbl rewrite project-name` no longer marks its rename commit as autogenerated, so changelog coverage asks for the breaking entry the closing message prints (its runnable `rlsbl changelog add` line names that commit); the transition-record commit stays autogenerated.

`rlsbl monorepo rename-releasable` no longer marks its rename commit as autogenerated, and its closing message now prints a runnable `(cd <member> && rlsbl changelog add ... --type breaking)` line naming that commit, which clears the changelog coverage it asks for.

`rlsbl release backfill --version <v> --commit <sha>` records the commit a version shipped from on its archive marked `unrecoverable`: it verifies the commit is an ancestor of HEAD and that every target in the release scope declares the version at that commit (a workspace releasable: its version file), then clears the mark and records the commit and tree hashes. An archive not marked unrecoverable is refused, so a recorded commit is never overwritten; at a workspace root `--releasable <name>` selects the releasable.

`rlsbl rewrite project-name` now refuses, before writing anything, when there is a Go target and the latest release is marked `unrecoverable`, instead of renaming with no `go-module-path` event; the error names `rlsbl release backfill --version <v> --commit <sha>` to record the commit that release shipped from.
